name: InMemory.Net
tagline: Commercial in-memory columnar SQL engine for .NET that speeds up reporting over hundreds of millions of rows.
description: InMemory.Net is a small commercial analytics database from Cork, Ireland, written in .NET. Its IRDBImport tool pulls data out of ODBC, OLE DB or .NET data providers, dictionary-compresses each column (typically 5-10x) into files on disk, and the IRDB server loads those files into RAM and answers SQL aggregations, with queries compiled to .NET code via Roslyn. It is essentially an extract-and-accelerate layer for reports and dashboards rather than a system of record: data is refreshed by re-importing, not by OLTP writes. Development is slow but alive; builds target .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET, and Parquet import and export arrived in 2025.

pricing.notes: Per-server licenses priced by named users ($400 for 1 user to $6,500 unlimited); SaaS hosting at $400 per backend server per month; OEM by quote.

scale.notes: Single server; capacity bounded by RAM after column compression.

strengths: Aggregates hundreds of millions of rows in about a second on one server
Dictionary-encoded columns shrink data 5-10x so large extracts fit in RAM
Imports from any ODBC, OLE DB or .NET source and from Parquet files
Native .NET API and LINQ for embedding fast analytics in .NET apps
Simple perpetual pricing compared with enterprise analytics engines
weaknesses: Batch re-import model; not designed for transactional writes
Windows/.NET only, single-node, small vendor with sparse documentation
Little community, tooling or third-party integration compared with DuckDB or ClickHouse
useCases: Accelerating slow SQL Server or ODBC-backed reports
Interactive dashboards over tens of millions of rows on a desktop
notIdealFor: Multi-terabyte datasets that exceed one machine's memory
